edbDesc: A process whereby atoms are ejected from a solid target material due to bombardment of the target by energetic ions. It is commonly used for thin-film deposition, etching and analytical techniques
title: Sputtering
description: Charged gas atoms slammed into a metal plate knock atoms loose, which then settle as a thin, even coating on anything nearby. Grove noticed metal from the cathode of a glow discharge tube coating the glass in 1852; today it lays down the films on hard disks, microchips and energy-saving window glass.
effect: fast ions knock atoms off a surface so they coat nearby objects
strength: Each incoming ion knocks off roughly one atom, so coatings grow slowly, a few nanometres per second, but are extremely even.
pickWhy: Specific, named effect behind most thin-film coating; Grove's 1852 observation is the standard origin.
